short: operators that take relations and return a relation: selection, projection, product, join, union, difference, rename. every query compiles into a tree of them.
the algebra's σ: keep the rows where a condition holds. WHERE in SQL, usually a Filter inside a scan in a plan.
the algebra's π: keep some columns. a set in the algebra, so SQL needs DISTINCT to match it.
the tree of words the parser builds from your text, checked against the grammar and nothing else.
the parse tree after analysis: every name replaced by an oid from the catalog. what views are stored as.
the stage that looks every name in a query up in the catalog. 'does not exist' errors come from here.
the stage that applies rules from pg_rewrite, which is how a view in FROM becomes its own query.
the tables that describe every object in the database: pg_class, pg_attribute, pg_type, pg_namespace and more.
object identifier: the number every catalog row has. after analysis, postgres refers to tables, types and functions by it.
a type that turns a table name into its oid through the search_path, and prints an oid as a name.
one operator in a plan, like a Seq Scan or a Hash Join. each answers its parent's request for the next row.
the first number in cost=a..b: the planner's estimate of the work before a node can return its first row.
the second number in cost=a..b: the estimated work to return every row, children included, in units of one sequential page read.
EXPLAIN that runs the query and prints actual rows, loops and buffers next to every estimate. it really executes DML.
how many times a plan node was run. actual rows is per loop, so the total is rows × loops.
a page EXPLAIN found already in shared buffers. a read had to be asked of the operating system.
every plan node answers next() with one row, pulling from its children, so rows flow up the plan one at a time.
a plan node that reads all of its input before returning a row: a Sort, a Hash, a HashAggregate.
reading every page of a table in order and testing every row.
walking an index and fetching each matching row from the table as it goes, in index order.
collect matching row addresses from indexes into a bitmap, then read each table page once, in order.
a bitmap that ran out of work_mem and only remembers pages, not rows, so every row on them is rechecked.
a join that runs its inner side once for every outer row. the only join for non-equality conditions.
a cache between a nested loop and its inner side, keyed on the join value. hits skip the lookup.
a plan node that keeps its child's rows so they can be read again without redoing the work below.
build a hash table on the smaller input, then probe it with each row of the bigger one. equality only.
a slice of a hash join's or hash aggregate's input, split off by hash when the table doesn't fit in memory and parked in a temp file.
how many times work_mem a hash table may use. 2 by default since postgres 15.
walk two inputs sorted on the join key with two cursors, stepping back over runs of equal keys.
the memory each sort or hash in a plan may use before it spills to disk. 4MB by default, per operation.
a sort too big for work_mem: sorted runs written to temp files, then merged.
the sort a LIMIT gets: keep only the best n rows in a heap while reading everything.
sorting input that's already sorted on the leading keys, one group at a time. it can stop early under a LIMIT.
GROUP BY with a hash table, one entry per group. any input order; everything comes out at the end.
GROUP BY over input sorted on the group key: each group comes out as soon as the key changes.
an aggregate split into a Partial step per piece (worker or partition) and a Finalize step that combines them.
the plan node that starts parallel workers and collects their rows. Gather Merge keeps them sorted.
a background process that runs part of a plan for a parallel query, next to the leader.
